summary.title: Trunk-based Development | Atlassian
summary.one_liner: Trunk-based development means developers merge small, frequent changes into a shared main branch, which supports CI/CD and simpler releases compared with long-lived Gitflow feature branches.
keywords: how to avoid long-lived feature branches
takeaways: Trunk-based development has developers merge small, frequent updates into one main branch, which is a requirement for continuous integration.
Gitflow uses long-lived feature branches and several primary branches, which increases merge conflicts and complexity compared with trunk-based development.
Feature flags let developers commit unfinished features directly to the main branch inside an inactive code path.
Best practices include small batches, automated testing, immediate code review, deleting merged branches, keeping three or fewer active branches, and merging to trunk at least daily.
summary.summary: This Atlassian article explains trunk-based development as a version control practice where developers merge small, frequent changes into a core trunk or main branch. It compares the model with Gitflow, which relies on long-lived feature branches and multiple primary branches, and argues that trunk-based development reduces merge conflicts and enables continuous integration. It then covers benefits such as continuous integration, code review, and daily releases, followed by best practices like feature flags, automated testing, and small batch commits. The page ends with a promotional note about Bitbucket's CI/CD features.
